summary: Sumi Lee is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She earned an MA at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign under Alexander L. Mayer and a PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles, supervised by Robert E. Buswell Jr.

Sumitra Mangesh Katre (1906–1998) worked in linguistics and Indology, earning a PhD from the University of London (~1928–1931). He held posts at Sir Parashurambhau College, Deccan College as Chair of Indo-European Philology (1942–1971), and the University of Texas at Austin.

Sun-Ah Choi is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Chicago under doctoral supervisor Juhyung Rhi, also studying under Richard Neer, Robert S. Nelson, Jaś Elsner, and Aden Kumler.

Sung Bae Park (born 1933) is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied under Lewis Lancaster (~1972–1979). He served as assistant professor at Dongguk University (~1968–1972) and held a post at Stony Brook University beginning in 1977.

Sungdoo Ahn specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Hamburg in 2001 under Lambert Schmithausen, later serving as Director at Geumgang University and Professor at Seoul National University (attested 2013).
Sungtaek Cho (born 1957) is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Stony Brook University and at Korea University, where he served as Director (attested 2012–2013).
Sunhee Kim completed a Doctor of Philosophy in Performance Practice at the University of Exeter under the supervision of Phillip B. Zarrilli.

Suniti Kumar Chatterji (1890–1977) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Calcutta, London, and Paris. He held posts at the University of Calcutta (~1914–1952) and served as National Professor in Humanities for the Government of India (~1965–1977).
Surama Dasgupta (1907–1998) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. She completed an MA and PhD at the University of Calcutta and earned a second PhD at the University of Cambridge.
Surendra Man Bajracharya is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Tribhuvan University under doctoral supervisor Bhadra Ratna Bajracharya and co-supervisor Ranjana Bajracharya.

Surendranath Dasgupta (1887–1952) worked in philosophy and Indology, earning PhDs from Calcutta and Cambridge. He held posts at Cambridge, Presidency University, Sanskrit College as Principal (~1931–1942), and Calcutta University as Chair of Philosophy (~1942–1945).

Suryya Kumar Bhuyan (1894–1964) was an Indology and history scholar. He studied at Cotton University, Presidency University, Kolkata, and the University of Calcutta (~1913–1916), later serving as a professor at Cotton University (attested 1956).
Susan Andrews is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned her PhD at Columbia University under the doctoral supervision of Chun-fang Yu.
Susan J. Rosenfield is an Indologist who completed her PhD at Harvard University in 2004, studying under faculty including Stephanie W. Jamison and George L. Hart.

Susan L. Huntington (born 1943) is an art historian and Indologist who worked in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She served as a professor at Ohio State University from approximately 1973 to 2011.

Susan Naquin (born 1944) is a scholar of Sinology, history, and archaeology. She served as a professor at the University of Pennsylvania (~1976–1993) and held a post at Princeton University (~1993–2013).

Susan Neiman (born 1955) is a philosopher who studied at Harvard and the Free University of Berlin. She held academic posts at Yale University (~1989–1996) and Tel Aviv University (~1996–2000), and joined the Einstein Forum around 2000.
Susan Niditch (born 1950) is a religious studies scholar who spent her career at Amherst College, serving in the religion department from approximately 1978 to 2020.

Susan Whitfield (born 1960) specializes in history, archaeology, and Sinology. After studying at SOAS University of London (~1986–1995), she directed the International Dunhuang Project at the British Library (1993–2017) and joined the University of East Anglia (~2018).

Susanne Hoeber Rudolph (1930–2015) was an Indology scholar who studied at Sarah Lawrence College, Radcliffe College, and Harvard University. She held academic posts at Harvard University (~1954–1964) and the University of Chicago (~1964–2002).
